'''''Calotis dentex''''' commonly known as '''white burr-daisy''',<ref name="NPSR">{{cite book |last1=Fairley |first1=Alan |last2=Moore |first2=Philip |title=Native Plants of the Sydney Region |date=2010 |publisher=Jacana Books |isbn=978-1-74175-571-8|page=446}}</ref> is a flowering plant in the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is a small shrub with white daisy like flowers and grows in New South Wales and Queensland. 

==Description==
''Calotis dentex'' is an upright, perennial, multi-branched, understory shrub to {{cvt|80|cm}} high with smooth or slightly hairy, brown stems. The [[cauline]] leaves are lance to oblong-shaped, {{cvt|2-9|cm}} long, {{cvt|4-11|mm}} wide, margins variable, lobed, toothed, sometimes entire, [[sessile (botany)|sessile]] and with occasional hairs. The white, occasionally mauve flowers are borne on stalks up to {{cvt|5|cm}} long, {{cvt|7-13|mm}} in diameter, either singly or in a loose [[cyme (botany)|cyme]] from leaf axils and a yellow central disc {{cvt|5-10|mm}} in diameter. Flowering occurs from October to April and the fruit is a flattened, reddish brown [[cypsela (botany)|cypsela]] with several spines {{cvt|4-6|mm}} long.<ref name="NPSR">{{cite book |last1=Fairley |first1=Alan |last2=Moore |first2=Philip |title=Native Plants of the Sydney Region |date=2010 |publisher=Jacana Books |isbn=978-1-74175-571-8|page=446}}</ref><ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |last1=Everett |first1=J. |title=''Calotis dentex'' |url=https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Calotis~dentex |website=PlantNET-NSW Flora online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Sydney |access-date=16 November 2024}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Calotis dentex'' was first formally described in 1820 by [[R.Br.|Robert Brown]] and the description was published in ''Consisting of Coloured Figures of Exotic Plants, Cultivated in British Gardens; with their History and Mode of Treatment''and the [[Type (biology)#Type specimen|type specimen]] was collected at [[Sydney]] by Robert Brown. The [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] "dentex" refers to the toothed edges of the leaves.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/rest/name/apni/100980/api/apni-format|title=''Calotis dentex''|author = |work=Vascular Plants Australian Plant Name Index (APNI)|access-date=2021-09-21}}</ref><ref>Les Robinson - Field Guide to the Native Plants of Sydney, {{ISBN|978-0-7318-1211-0}} page 132</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
White burr-daisy grows mostly on clay soils in grasslands and open forests in New South Wales and Queensland.<ref name="NPSR"/>
